prompt: What is special about the Giza pyramids?
answer:
Offline knowledge preview (not an LLM response). An AI provider must be configured on the server for conversational answers.

Pyramids of Giza — The Giza plateau is home to the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure and their surrounding ancient monuments. The Great Pyramid of Khufu dates to Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, roughly 4,500 years ago, and was the tallest human-made structure for many centuries. The site is part of the UNESCO listing for Memphis and its Necropolis. The plateau is large and mostly open desert, so a visit involves a lot of walking in the sun.

Saqqara Step Pyramid — The Step Pyramid of Djoser is part of the extensive ancient necropolis at Saqqara. The Step Pyramid of Djoser, from the Third Dynasty, is often described as one of the earliest large stone monuments in the world and is associated with the architect Imhotep. Saqqara lies about 30 km south of the Giza plateau, so it needs its own travel time. The necropolis has many other tombs and pyramids.

Great Sphinx of Giza — The limestone Great Sphinx stands on the Giza plateau, with a lion's body and a human head. The Sphinx is carved directly out of the limestone bedrock and is commonly attributed to the reign of Khafre. It is around 70 metres long. It is usually visited together with the pyramids, in the same area.

Grand Egyptian Museum — A major archaeological museum near the Giza pyramids dedicated to ancient Egyptian heritage. The museum is built close to the pyramids and is designed to display a very large collection of ancient Egyptian artefacts, including objects associated with Tutankhamun. Its size means a full visit takes several hours. Which galleries are open can change, so check the official site.

Karnak Temple Complex — A vast ancient Egyptian temple complex and part of the UNESCO-listed site of Ancient Thebes. Karnak was built and expanded over roughly two thousand years by many pharaohs. Its Great Hypostyle Hall contains a forest of 134 huge columns. The complex was dedicated mainly to the god Amun and is linked in antiquity to Luxor Temple by an avenue of sphinxes.

Luxor Temple — A major temple on the east bank of the Nile, linked in antiquity with Karnak. Temple of Hatshepsut — A striking terraced mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari dedicated to Queen Hatshepsut. The temple was built into the cliffs at Deir el-Bahari for Queen Hatshepsut of the 18th Dynasty. Its colonnaded terraces are one of the best-known pieces of ancient Egyptian architecture. It is on the west bank, close to the Valley of the Kings.

Philae Temple — An island temple complex dedicated chiefly to Isis, relocated during the Nubian monument rescue campaign. The temple complex was dismantled and rebuilt on higher ground on Agilkia Island when the Aswan High Dam threatened to submerge it. Visitors reach it by short boat ride. It is dedicated mainly to the goddess Isis.
